changelog: - **Undo after Export ▸ Project revision no longer takes the document off the revision just written.** Every undo step remembers which project revision the document was on, so that undoing an applied proposal brings the earlier revision back with it. An export moved the document to its new revision without telling the steps taken before it, so Ctrl+Z after an export brought the older state back: a plain document that had just become a project was no project again (the revision chip went away, also after a reload, and the next export began a different project than the file just written), and an open revision went back to its parent, so that the next export was a sibling of the file just written, not its successor. Redo did the same for a step undone before the export. Undo and redo now only move the content: the document stays on the exported revision and is marked unsaved when its content differs from the file. Exporting again with nothing changed leaves everything as it is, and an applied proposal that has no export after it is undone and redone with its revision as before.
